title: 5 months trekking through South America
excerpt: Solo travelling with a personal item sized bag — how I packed for 5 months, and why.
content:
With research and experimentation, you can pack less!

Almost every year I plan 3 or 4 month long adventures to explore remote trails around the world and I'm taking off soon on my longest trip yet, 5 months!

When a carry-on sized item was included in most economy tickets, I'd take my favourite pastel roller bag onto the planes, a backpack and a pillow case stuffed with extra clothing. Now that base fares only include a personal sized item, I'll be taking just a small backpack, fanny pack and neck pillow case stuffed with smaller items.

What you decide to bring depends on where you're going, the climate and weather, what you'll be doing and your personal preferences. I've packed and repacked almost 20 times in the last 3 months, narrowing down my must-haves for trekking in South America — see the full pack list and rationale.

The benefits of travelling with JUST a personal item sized bag include:

  1. Avoiding airline baggage fees
  2. Saving time at the airport
  3. Zero lost bag anxiety
  4. Reducing daily decision fatigue
  5. Appearing less touristy

I went for a bag that would fit in the smallest of budget airline baggage sizers and that would hold its shape when fully loaded, the Sherpani Soleil. Light material like merino wool reduces the overall weight of the bag, as does holding heavier items like battery packs in a fanny pack or on your person in some other way. I try to avoid packing liquids for the same reason.

No matter what, the only shoes you can bring are the ones on your feet! I'm obsessed with Hoka's Hopara line of all purpose hiking shoes. They're waterproof and I've run, walked endlessly and summited mountains in them.

All of this already feels like an accomplishment and I can't wait to see if I've made all the right decisions or what I'd change for next time. Was every item packed used? Did the compression bag hold up? Was it possible to remain organized?

Dear diary:

How are you feeling right now?

Only 10 days before I'll be falling asleep in Mexico City, starting several adventures of a lifetime again. On the one hand, 5 months feels unfathomable. On the other hand, I know it's going to fly by and I'll be back to my vibrator and weed in no time. Coming back to essential oil diffusers, warm baths, Lenige lip masks and Aesop hand cream are experiences I will greatly anticipate upon return. Not to mention snuggling my cat again when she comes back for my birthday month and the opening of my balcony space with the sun's return to it.

Life is good. I am lucky. This is so many dreams come true and my ideal lifestyle. I'm not employed but it's a gift to be in this millennial pause or mid-career retirement, whatever you want to call it, while I have the good health and energy to see more of the beautiful world. I have to believe what's meant to happen will and that I am making all the right moves to reveal my future opportunities.
